title: Brand families in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about the big groups behind the brands we buy every day, and how they are organised.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are, not just on what you think.

outro.heading: Who owns what is rarely obvious.
paras: Most shoppers never think about the company behind a name, but the way a group arranges its brands shapes prices, menus, shops and jobs.
Today, think about what shoppers, franchisees and owners each want from a brand.

questions.q: Volkswagen Group owns many vehicle brands. Which of these does it NOT own?
questions.explain: Rolls-Royce cars belong to BMW, which also owns Mini. Volkswagen Group owns Audi, Porsche, Bentley, Lamborghini, Škoda, SEAT, Cupra and the motorbike maker Ducati, among others.
questions.source: Volkswagen Group / BMW Group company information

questions.q: Roughly how many brands does Nestlé own?
questions.explain: More than 2,000, from KitKat and Nescafé to brands sold in just one country. Only some of them carry the Nestlé name on the pack.

questions.q: What share of McDonald's restaurants worldwide are run by franchisees rather than by the company itself?
questions.explain: About 95% of the 45,356 restaurants open at the end of 2025. McDonald's earns much of its money from franchisees' rent and royalties, not from selling burgers itself.

questions.q: In the UK, which chain has more outlets: the bakery Greggs or McDonald's?
questions.explain: Greggs, by a long way: about 2,740 shops at the end of 2025 (including about 600 run by franchise partners), against about 1,600 McDonald's restaurants in the UK and Ireland together.
questions.source: Greggs plc, 2025 full-year results (reported by The Caterer); McDonald's, Restaurants by Market 2025

questions.q: Marriott International runs hotels under many different brand names, from Ritz-Carlton to Moxy. Roughly how many?
questions.explain: More than 30 brands, each aimed at a different guest and price. Most guests never notice that so many belong to one group.

questions.q: In which year did Kentucky Fried Chicken officially shorten its name to KFC?
questions.explain: 1991. The company said it simply wanted a shorter name; many observers think it also helped to play down the word 'fried', though KFC never said so.
questions.source: KFC / Yum! Brands company history; The Takeout, 2025

questions.q: Pret A Manger, Panera Bread and Krispy Kreme (a large stake) have all belonged to the same investor. Who?
options: JAB Holding, the Reimann family's firm
questions.explain: JAB, the investment firm of the German Reimann family. It bought Pret in 2018 for a reported £1.5 billion including debt, adding it to a portfolio that already included Panera and Krispy Kreme.
questions.source: BakeryAndSnacks.com / Bloomberg, May 2018 (price reported; terms not disclosed)

questions.q: In 2025 the US delivery company DoorDash completed its purchase of Deliveroo. For roughly how much?
questions.explain: About £2.9 billion, agreed in May 2025 and completed in October. Deliveroo had floated on the London Stock Exchange in 2021 at a value of about £7.6 billion.
questions.source: DoorDash / Deliveroo, offer announcement, May 2025; ITV News, March 2021
